title: Know where your money goes
summary: Writing down what you spend shows patterns that help you make better choices.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Dev gets ₹300 a month and feels it vanishes. His teacher suggests a simple habit: write down every spend in a small notebook.

For one month, Dev notes each item. Canteen snacks ₹20, ₹30, ₹20. Notebook ₹40. Birthday gift ₹100. Online game top-up ₹50. This is **recording spending**: capturing every rupee, even tiny ones.

At month end he adds it up by type. Snacks come to ₹120, which is far more than he expected. That is **spotting patterns**: seeing where money keeps going.

Now Dev has real facts, not guesses. He decides to bring snacks from home twice a week. He is not punishing himself. He is choosing with clear information.

You can also track using a phone note or a family diary. What matters is doing it regularly, in a place you can find again.

Tracking is the first step. Once you can see your spending, you can plan it.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.
